messages:
Priya: Heads-up — customer onboarding reported a p99 spike on /v1/generate around 09:12 UTC. p95 jumped ~120ms -> 520ms, p99 ~700ms -> 2.3s. Ticket #12345. Seeing lots of slow tail latency in their calls.

Alex: Looking at infra dashboards now — prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate went from ~8% to ~62% between 09:08–09:16. Eviction_count spiked. No runtime deploys logged.

Priya: No deploys on runtime during that window. Autoscaler did scale up a bunch of small nodes at ~09:05. Could be warmup problem after new nodes join.

Mira: Found repeated log lines that look like the same logical prefix but different cache keys (trailing spaces / punctuation differences). Suspect a key-normalization bug in the prefix cache layer. Example logs:

```
[09:11:34] prefix_cache MISS key="user:acct:1234:prompt:hello"
[09:11:34] prefix_cache MISS key="user:acct:1234:prompt:hello "  <-- note trailing space
[09:11:34] prefix_cache MISS key="user:acct:1234:prompt:hello\n" <-- newline suffix from client
```

Sam: Repro steps I ran locally: run the load generator hitting the same logical prompts but with small whitespace/noise variations and you'll see miss_rate climb. Command I used:

```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -sS -X POST $API -d '{"prompt":"hello'$((i%3==0?" ":""))'}' & done
```

Sam: Also saw request headers from one client that had inconsistent content-length calculation which can produce extra \r or trailing space in the body.

Jorge: Immediate mitigations: (1) hotfix key normalization (trim/normalize whitespace, unify tokenization), (2) increase prefix cache capacity temporarily to absorb thrash, (3) run a cache-warm job for affected prefixes, (4) optionally route heavy onboarding traffic to dedicated pool until warm.

Alex: I have a small PR that normalizes keys (trim + collapse multiple spaces). Will run it on canary nodes. Config tweak suggestion: prefix_cache.max_entries 50k -> 200k for 1h window; reduce eviction aggressiveness.

ops-bot: Incident INC-789 created and oncall paged.

Priya: Plan: 1) deploy key-normalize patch to 10% canary, 2) run warmup script for known customer prefixes, 3) monitor p95/p99 + miss_rate, 4) if stable, roll to 100% and revert autoscaler change if still problematic. I'll kick off warmup now.

Sam: Warmup script (simple curl-based):
```
# warmup-prefixes.sh
for p in $(cat prefixes.txt); do
  curl -s -X POST $API -d "{\"prompt\": \"$p\"}" > /dev/null
  sleep 0.01
done
```

Mira: Added a Grafana alert: prefix_kv_cache.miss_rate > 20% for 5m -> page. Also added a panel for normalized_key distribution to detect anomalies.

Alex: Hotfix is running on canary. Early signal: canary p95 dropped from 520ms -> 160ms, p99 reduced similarly. Miss rate dropped to <10% on canary traffic.

Priya: Good. Rolling patch to remaining fleet tonight at 02:00 UTC, coordinating with oncall. Will also add unit tests for key normalization and an e2e that asserts stable cache hit rates for a synthetic workload.

Jorge: Nice. After roll, follow-ups: (a) add a cache-key sanitizer in the public SDKs to help clients, (b) add histogram for key entropy to detect random/noisy prefixes, (c) review autoscaler warmup policy so new nodes pre-seed hot prefixes.

Alex: Agree. I'll open follow-up tickets for SDK sanitizer + autoscaler warmup.

Priya: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the action log. Updating ticket #12345 with mitigation steps and timeline. :thumbsup:
